title: A Second-Order Cepstral Signature of Contact-Vibration Sounds Reproduced by Laptop Loudspeakers: A Synthetic Case Study
summary: A mobile phone vibrating on a hard surface often sounds qualitatively unlike ordinary audiovisual recordings when reproduced through laptop loudspeakers. We propose that part of this perceptual distinctiveness can be described as a nested periodicity: a first-order cepstral structure reflecting the vibration period and its multiples, and a second-order cepstral structure reflecting repeated spacing within the first-order cepstrum.
